title: The effect of additive engineering and machine learning on high performance perovskite solar cells
summary: Additive engineering has emerged as a powerful strategy for enhancing the efficiency and stability of perovskite solar cells (PSCs), enabling precise control over crystallization kinetics, defect passivation, interfacial energetics, and long-term environmental stability. By controlling nucleation and crystal growth, and thereby optimizing film morphology, additives effectively suppress non-radiative recombination and ion migration, addressing key challenges in the path toward commercialization. However, the conventional discovery process remains largely empirical and time-consuming. The integration of machine learning (ML) offers a promising avenue for data-driven screening, rational molecular design, and accelerated optimization of additive systems. ML models trained on experimental datasets and augmented with density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations can predict interactions between additives and perovskites, identify performance-determining descriptors, and guide the discovery of novel functional molecules. This review systematically outlines the multifaceted roles of additives in PSCs, from crystallization regulation to interfacial stabilization. We further highlight the synergy between ML and additive engineering, emphasizing its potential to establish a predictive, intelligent framework for next-generation photovoltaic materials.

screen.tldr: Review of additive engineering in perovskite solar cells and how machine learning can screen additives, predict interactions, and guide rational molecular design.
screen.transfer_note: ML-guided screening and descriptor learning for additives could transfer to crystal-growth control and polymorph stabilization in organic CSP.

AI.tldr: The abstract reviews how additives improve perovskite solar cells and argues that machine learning can accelerate additive discovery and optimization.
AI.motivation: Perovskite solar cells still face key bottlenecks in efficiency, stability, defect control, and ion migration. Traditional additive discovery is empirical and slow, so a more predictive and data-driven approach is needed.
AI.method: The paper is a review that synthesizes additive engineering strategies in PSCs, covering crystallization control, defect passivation, interfacial energetics, and environmental stability. It also discusses machine learning approaches trained on experimental data and supported by density functional theory and molecular dynamics to predict additive-perovskite interactions and guide molecular design.
AI.result: The review shows that additives can improve film morphology, suppress non-radiative recombination, reduce ion migration, and enhance long-term stability. AI.conclusion: Additive engineering is a powerful route to better PSC performance, and combining it with machine learning could enable a predictive framework for rational design of next-generation photovoltaic materials.

title: 1-Dodecyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl) imide Interface Design for Stable and Effective Perovskite Solar Cells.
summary: Power conversion efficiency (PCE) is limited by the high density of defects and poor energy level alignment of the SnO2/perovskite (PVK) buried interface in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Herein, a synergistic molecular interface engineering strategy is designed by using an ionic liquid, 1-dodecyl-3-methylimidazolium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl) imide salt (DMIMTFSI) to modify this critical interface. The strong electron-withdrawing TFSI- anion induces a downward shift of the conduction band of SnO2, thereby optimizing energy level alignment and facilitating electron extraction. Meanwhile, the DMIM+ cation passivates interfacial defects through robust chemical interactions with Pb2+ and I- ions. Furthermore, the long alkyl chain of DMIMTFSI templates the formation of an ordered porous PbI2 morphology, which improves the crystallinity of the overlying PVK film. The DMIMTFSI modification reduces the trap-state density by 31.86%, prolongs the carrier lifetime by 39.42%, and increases the built-in potential from 0.95 to 1.02 V. Therefore, the DMIMTFSI-modified device achieves a PCE of 24.14%, significantly outperforming the pristine device of 22.34%. The unencapsulated modified device retained 87% of its initial PCE after being stored for 1000 h under ambient conditions, demonstrating excellent environmental stability. This work provides a viable multifunctional interface engineering pathway toward high-performance and stable PSCs.

screen.tldr: Ionic-liquid interface engineering improves SnO2/perovskite alignment, passivates defects, and templates better perovskite crystallinity for more efficient, stable solar cells.
screen.transfer_note: Interface passivation and crystallization-control strategies could inspire defect-aware surface engineering in crystal growth and thin-film polymorph control.

AI.tldr: An ionic liquid, DMIMTFSI, is used to engineer the SnO2/perovskite buried interface in PSCs, simultaneously improving energy alignment, defect passivation, and perovskite film quality, which boosts efficiency and stability.
AI.motivation: The SnO2/perovskite buried interface suffers from high defect density and poor band alignment, which limits charge extraction, increases recombination, and suppresses power conversion efficiency.
AI.method: A synergistic molecular interface engineering strategy was applied using the ionic liquid DMIMTFSI. The TFSI anion lowers the SnO2 conduction band, while the DMIM cation passivates interfacial defects via interactions with Pb2+ and I-. The long alkyl chain also templates an ordered porous PbI2 morphology to improve subsequent perovskite crystallization.
AI.result: The modification reduced trap-state density by 31.86%, increased carrier lifetime by 39.42%, and raised built-in potential from 0.95 to 1.02 V. The device PCE improved from 22.34% to 24.14%. The unencapsulated device retained 87% of its initial PCE after 1000 h in ambient storage.
AI.conclusion: DMIMTFSI provides a multifunctional interface engineering approach that enhances interfacial energetics, defect control, film quality, efficiency, and operational stability in perovskite solar cells.

title: Enhancing carrier transport in Cs2AgBiBr6 double perovskites through multifunctional ferroelectric polymer doping
summary: Cs2AgBiBr6 lead-free double perovskites are promising materials for optoelectronic applications but suffer from limited carrier transport due to defects and strong electron–phonon coupling. In this work, we introduce a multifunctional doping strategy using the ferroelectric polymer polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) to simultaneously address these challenges. PVDF modulates film crystallization to reduce defects, relaxes lattice strain to weaken electron–phonon coupling, and—after electrical polarization—provides a built-in electric field that promotes charge separation. As a result, PVDF-doped Cs2AgBiBr6 solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 1.91%, representing a 40% improvement over the control device (1.36%), with much improved stability. This work presents a simple and effective approach to improving carrier dynamics in double perovskites for broader optoelectronic applications.

screen.tldr: PVDF doping improves crystallization, strain, and charge separation in Cs2AgBiBr6 double perovskite solar cells, boosting efficiency and stability.

AI.tldr: A ferroelectric polymer doping strategy using PVDF improves Cs2AgBiBr6 double perovskite solar cells by reducing defects, easing lattice strain, and creating a built-in field after polarization, raising efficiency to 1.91% and improving stability.
AI.motivation: Lead-free double perovskites such as Cs2AgBiBr6 are attractive for optoelectronics, but their performance is limited by defect-related carrier losses and strong electron–phonon coupling, which hinder charge transport and device efficiency.
AI.method: The authors introduced polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) into Cs2AgBiBr6 films as a multifunctional dopant. PVDF was used to control crystallization, reduce defect density, relax lattice strain, and, after electrical polarization, generate an internal electric field to assist charge separation.
AI.result: PVDF-doped devices reached a champion power conversion efficiency of 1.91%, compared with 1.36% for the control, corresponding to a 40% relative improvement. The devices also showed markedly improved stability.
AI.conclusion: PVDF provides a simple and effective route to simultaneously improve film quality, carrier dynamics, and interfacial charge separation in lead-free double perovskites, making it a promising strategy for broader optoelectronic applications.
